newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes higher on yen/dollar movement.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes higher on yen/dollar movement.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Wednesday as exporters sold dollars and the U.S. currency fell against the yen in world markets, dealers said.
"Dollar sales by domestic companies for export negotiations boosted the won," said one bank dealer. "A falling dollar in world markets also affected the won/dollar rate."
The won ended at 895.00 compared with Tuesday's closing of 896.50. It hit a low of 896.70 on speculative dollar buying.
"There was a tug-of-war between longs and shorts as dealers differed in their views over the future market direction," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

Dealers said the won would not fall below the key 900 level in the near-term since the government was determined to stop its sharp depreciation. But the won was not likely to rise much because of weak economic fundamentals.
"The dollar is in consolidation following steep rises last month," said the dealer at the foreign bank.

The domestic bank dealer said the won would open strong on Thursday but would fall on advanced dollar buying on looming importer deals next week. "But the dollar will not rise over the 897.00 won level," he said. Thursday's mid-rate is expected to be fixed at 895.80 against 896.20 today. -- Y. J. Yeom
